articles.title: Impact of preoperative osteoporosis on short- and long-term complications following ankle ORIF: A multi-institutional propensity-matched analysis.
articles.authors: Horani K, Lawand J, Wang J, Cione N, Ghali A, Ruelos VCB, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing ankle ORIF with at least 2 years follow-up
articles.sample_size: 4190 matched patients (with and without preoperative osteoporosis)
articles.outcomes: Device infection, DVT, transfusion requirement at 90 days; device infection and hardware removal at 2 years
articles.take_home: Patients with osteoporosis who have ankle fracture surgery experience more complications in the short term, including infections and blood clots, and are more likely to need their hardware removed within 2 years. The study suggests optimising bone health and using appropriate fixation methods for osteoporotic bone after surgery may help reduce these problems.
